cards.heading: A wildcard is an inverted mask
cards.body: In a wildcard mask a 0 bit means 'this bit must match' and a 1 bit means 'don't care'. To match a whole subnet, subtract its subnet mask from 255.255.255.255, octet by octet.

cards.heading: Reading a wildcard as a range
cards.body: Add the wildcard to the base address to get the last address matched. Everything from the base address up to there matches.

cards.heading: host and any
cards.body: Two shortcuts appear everywhere. 'host A' means exactly one address (wildcard 0.0.0.0). 'any' means every address (0.0.0.0 with wildcard 255.255.255.255).

cards.heading: Not just ACLs
cards.body: OSPF network statements use wildcards the same way: they choose which interfaces join OSPF. The logic is the same, so practising one helps with the other.
